The guide to buying and selling between countries. 24/24 ONE WORLD does not file customs declarations: a licensed customs broker (freight forwarder) can do it for you.
Market Access Map (ITC, UN-WTO): duties and rules for almost every country
Access2Markets (European Union): duties, taxes, rules of origin, step by step
TARIC: customs code (HS code) and duties when entering the European Union
Transport document: bill of lading (sea), air waybill (air), CMR (road)
Certificate of origin (to get reduced duties)
EORI number (businesses importing or exporting in the EU)
Depending on the product: health or phytosanitary certificate, licence, CE standards
EXW: the buyer handles everything from the seller's factory.
FCA: the seller hands the export-cleared goods to the buyer's carrier.
FOB: the seller loads onto the ship; after that, risks and costs are the buyer's.
CIF: the seller pays freight and insurance to the port of arrival.
DAP: the seller delivers to destination, the buyer pays import duties.
DDP: the seller pays everything, import duties included.
Banned or controlled everywhere: weapons, drugs, counterfeits, protected species (CITES), some medicines. Such listings are refused and can be reported (🚩).
